conditionals.notes: Encompasses B02 logical_operators and_or_not/combine_conditions, booleans.truthiness, none_type.check_for_none and arithmetic_operators.modulo_patterns as B02 requested. pass is introduced in if_statement KP4. Case-insensitive comparison of answers (.lower()) is left to B03 string_methods; the in operator for membership tests is B03/B06. try/except around int(input()) is B09 exceptions.

nested_conditionals.notes: flatten_nesting doubles as the 'guard clause' idea; early return as a guard is B05 return_values.

conditional_expressions.notes: One topic: only Helsinki teaches it, but it is core because B07 comprehensions and B08 lambdas use it.

match_statement.notes: Non-core (3 courses, introduced only). Only literal, |, _, capture and guard patterns are taught here; sequence patterns (case [x, y]) belong with B06 lists/unpacking, mapping patterns with B07 dictionaries, class patterns with the OOP batch. Python 3.10+ only. Reconciliation: every snippet was run with Python 3.13; all outputs were correct. Subject assignments and output comments were added to the fragments that lacked them, and the exact SyntaxError for a non-final capture case was quoted.

while_loops.notes: Validation that survives non-numeric input (try/except ValueError) is B09 exceptions. Random secret numbers (random.randint) are B13 random_module; guessing-game examples use a fixed secret. while True + break lives in break_continue.while_true_loops.

for_loops.notes: Without lists (B06) for loops iterate over range and strings only. for_loops.loop_over_characters has pending_prerequisites concept:strings because B03 runs in parallel; if B03 also wrote a 'traverse a string' topic the stitching pass should merge them (one should own it). Looping over lists, enumerate and zip are B06; looping over dict items is B07; looping over file lines is B10.

range_function.notes: range(n) itself is introduced in for_loops.repeat_n_times; this concept owns start/stop/step. list(range(...)), len(range) and membership in a range are B06.

break_continue.notes: loop_else is non-core (taught by no course but a real Python feature). Breaking out of nested loops via a function return is B05 return_values.

nested_loops.notes: grids_and_patterns is non-core because it depends on print_output.sep_and_end (non-core). Nested loops over 2D lists are B07 nested_data_structures; string repetition '#' * n as an alternative to the inner loop is B03 and could encompass grids_and_patterns. Reconciliation: grids_and_patterns is core now that print_output.sep_and_end is core.

loop_patterns.notes: Built-ins sum(), max(), min(), any(), all() that replace these loops are B05 builtin_functions, which should encompass the matching pattern topics. Counting with dictionaries is B07. Guess-and-check / exhaustive enumeration is its own concept (guess_and_check) in a later batch.

iteration.notes: One non-core topic. Custom iterators (__iter__/__next__) are B11 dunder_methods; generators and generator expressions are B08 generators; itertools is B07; enumerate/zip are B06. Reconciliation: iter_and_next promoted to core (generators build on it).

topics.title: Running code only when a condition is true: if
topics.summary: Write an if statement whose indented block runs only when its condition is True, and fix missing-colon and indentation errors.

knowledge_points.title: if runs its block only when the condition is True
knowledge_points.worked_example:
temp = 30
if temp > 25:
    print('Hot')
print('Done')
# Hot
# Done
With temp = 20 only Done is printed: the block is skipped when the condition is False.
knowledge_points.practice: Predict the output of a short if program for two or three different starting values.

knowledge_points.title: Indentation decides what is inside the block
knowledge_points.worked_example:
x = 5
if x > 10:
    print('big')
    print('really big')
print('end')
# end
Both indented lines are skipped together; the unindented line always runs.
knowledge_points.practice: Predict output where some lines are indented and some are not; reorder lines (Parsons) so only the right ones are conditional.

knowledge_points.title: Missing colons and missing indentation are errors
knowledge_points.worked_example:
if x > 10
    print('big')    # SyntaxError at the missing colon
if x > 10:
print('big')        # IndentationError: an indented block was expected
Every if line ends with a colon and is followed by at least one indented line.
knowledge_points.practice: Find and fix the syntax or indentation error in short if programs.

knowledge_points.title: Conditions stored in variables, and pass for an empty block
knowledge_points.worked_example:
rain_mm = 3
is_raining = rain_mm > 0
if is_raining:
    print('Take an umbrella')
if rain_mm > 50:
    pass  # handle storms later
pass is a statement that does nothing; a block cannot be empty.
knowledge_points.practice: Predict output when the condition is a Boolean variable; fix an if with an empty block.

topics.title: Choosing between two paths: if / else
topics.summary: Use else to run exactly one of two blocks, including the classic even/odd test with %.

knowledge_points.title: else runs when the condition is False
knowledge_points.worked_example:
age = 15
if age >= 18:
    print('adult')
else:
    print('minor')
# minor
Exactly one of the two blocks runs, never both and never neither.
knowledge_points.practice: Predict which branch runs for several inputs; fill in the missing condition or else line.

knowledge_points.title: Even or odd with %
knowledge_points.worked_example:
n = 7
if n % 2 == 0:
    print('even')
else:
    print('odd')
# odd
n % 2 is 0 exactly for even numbers.
knowledge_points.practice: Write if/else programs that classify numbers by divisibility (even/odd, multiple of 5 or not).

knowledge_points.title: Both branches can set the same variable
knowledge_points.worked_example:
hours = 45
rate = 10
if hours > 40:
    pay = 40 * rate + (hours - 40) * rate * 1.5
else:
    pay = hours * rate
print(pay)  # 475.0
Whichever branch runs, pay is defined afterwards.
knowledge_points.practice: Trace which branch runs and the final value of the variable; write an if/else that sets a shipping cost.

knowledge_points.title: else takes no condition and must line up with its if
knowledge_points.worked_example:
if x > 0:
    print('positive')
else x <= 0:      # SyntaxError: else has no condition
    print('not positive')
Write plain else: at the same indentation as the if.
knowledge_points.practice: Fix if/else programs with a condition on else, a misaligned else, or a missing colon.

topics.title: More than two choices: elif chains
topics.summary: Write if/elif/else chains, predict which single branch runs, order the tests correctly, and tell a chain apart from separate ifs.

knowledge_points.title: elif adds more choices
knowledge_points.practice: Predict the grade printed for several scores; write a chain that classifies a temperature into three bands.

knowledge_points.title: The first true branch wins; the rest are skipped
knowledge_points.worked_example:
score = 95
# same chain as above prints only A
95 >= 80 is also True, but once a branch runs the rest of the chain is skipped.
knowledge_points.practice: Predict output for values that satisfy several conditions in the chain.

knowledge_points.title: Order matters: test the narrowest condition first
knowledge_points.practice: Find and fix chains whose order makes a branch unreachable.

knowledge_points.title: Separate ifs vs one elif chain
knowledge_points.worked_example:
x = 15
if x > 10:
    print('big')
if x > 5:
    print('medium')
# big
# medium
Separate ifs are each tested; with elif only 'big' would print.
knowledge_points.practice: Predict output for the same tests written as separate ifs and as an elif chain; choose which form a task needs.

topics.title: Combining conditions in an if
topics.summary: Use and, or, not and chained comparisons in if conditions, and avoid the `x == 1 or 2` bug.

knowledge_points.title: and: both tests must pass
knowledge_points.worked_example:
age = 16
if age >= 13 and age <= 19:
    print('teen')
# same as: if 13 <= age <= 19:
One compound test replaces two nested checks.
knowledge_points.practice: Predict output for ages on and around the boundaries; write a range check both ways.

knowledge_points.title: or: any one alternative is enough
knowledge_points.practice: Write conditions that accept any of several values; predict output for inputs on both sides.

knowledge_points.title: The `x == 1 or 2` bug
knowledge_points.worked_example:
choice = 5
if choice == 1 or 2:
    print('valid')   # prints valid!
2 on its own is truthy, so the condition is always True. Write choice == 1 or choice == 2.
knowledge_points.practice: Predict what buggy or-conditions do; fix them.

knowledge_points.title: not and the 'outside the range' test
knowledge_points.worked_example:
x = 120
if not (0 <= x <= 100):
    print('out of range')
# same as: if x < 0 or x > 100:
knowledge_points.practice: Write the condition for 'outside a range' with not and with or; pick equivalent conditions from a list.

topics.title: Using truthiness and None in if
topics.summary: Write if conditions that rely on truthy/falsy values (if count:, if name:) and know when an explicit is None test is needed instead.

knowledge_points.title: if on a number: zero counts as false
knowledge_points.practice: Predict the branch taken for 0, negative and positive values; rewrite if count != 0: in the short form.

knowledge_points.title: if on text: the empty string counts as false
knowledge_points.practice: Predict output for '', ' ' and 'Ana'; write an if that uses a default when a name is empty.

knowledge_points.title: When 0 is a real value, test is None instead
knowledge_points.practice: Find and fix conditions that treat 0 or '' as missing; choose between truthiness and is None for described situations.

topics.title: Branching on what the user types
topics.summary: Write small programs that read input and branch on it, including menus, and fix the forgotten-int() and exact-text-match bugs.

knowledge_points.title: Read a number, then branch
knowledge_points.practice: Predict output for given typed inputs; write a program that reads a number and prints one of two messages.

knowledge_points.title: Comparing typed text is exact
knowledge_points.practice: Predict which branch runs for inputs differing in case or spacing.

knowledge_points.title: Forgetting int(): comparing text with a number
knowledge_points.worked_example:
n = input('n? ')
if n > 10:          # TypeError: str and int cannot be compared with >
    print('big')
if n == 10: is never True either, because '10' == 10 is False. Convert first: n = int(input('n? ')).
knowledge_points.practice: Fix input programs that compare raw input with numbers; predict whether they crash or take a wrong branch.

knowledge_points.title: Menu programs with a catch-all else
knowledge_points.practice: Write a menu program for a given spec; predict output for valid and invalid choices.

topics.title: if statements inside if statements
topics.summary: Trace and write nested if/else statements, using indentation to tell which else belongs to which if.

knowledge_points.title: The inner if is only checked when the outer one is true
knowledge_points.practice: Predict output for every combination of the two inputs; fill a trace table of which tests are evaluated.

knowledge_points.title: Indentation decides which if an else belongs to
knowledge_points.practice: Predict output for two programs that differ only in the indentation of else.

knowledge_points.title: Tracing a decision tree
knowledge_points.practice: Trace three-level decision trees (adventure-game style choices) for given inputs; write one from a flowchart.

topics.title: Flattening nested ifs with and and elif
topics.summary: Rewrite nested ifs as a single compound condition or an elif chain, and recognise when nesting is the clearer choice.

knowledge_points.title: Nested ifs with no else become one and
knowledge_points.practice: Rewrite nested ifs as one condition; choose which rewrites are equivalent.

knowledge_points.title: An if alone inside else becomes elif
knowledge_points.practice: Flatten else-if nesting into an elif chain; predict output of both versions to check they agree.

knowledge_points.title: Keep nesting when several branches share one outer test
knowledge_points.practice: Decide which of several programs should stay nested; spot a flattening that changed behaviour.

topics.title: One-line choices: value if condition else other
topics.summary: Write and read conditional expressions (a if cond else b), convert between them and if/else statements, and use them inside larger expressions.

knowledge_points.title: Pick one of two values in a single expression
knowledge_points.worked_example:
n = 7
label = 'even' if n % 2 == 0 else 'odd'
print(label)  # odd
The condition sits in the middle; the value before if is used when it is True.
knowledge_points.practice: Predict the value of conditional expressions; fill in the missing part.

knowledge_points.title: Converting between if/else and a conditional expression
knowledge_points.practice: Rewrite if/else assignments as one line and back.

knowledge_points.title: Using it inside other expressions
knowledge_points.worked_example:
n = 1
print(n, 'item' if n == 1 else 'items')  # 1 item
price = 20
total = price + (5 if n > 3 else 0)   # 20
Without the parentheses the whole sum would be inside the choice.
knowledge_points.practice: Predict output where the expression is an argument or part of arithmetic, with and without parentheses.

knowledge_points.title: else is required, and long chains hurt readability
knowledge_points.worked_example:
fee = 10 if age >= 18         # SyntaxError: the else part is missing
size = 'S' if n < 5 else 'M' if n < 10 else 'L'  # legal but hard to read
Prefer an if/elif statement for three or more choices.
knowledge_points.practice: Fix conditional expressions with a missing else; choose whether a task suits a conditional expression or a statement.

topics.title: Choosing by value with match and case
topics.summary: Write match statements with literal cases, | alternatives and a _ catch-all, and rewrite an elif chain on one variable as a match.

knowledge_points.title: match compares one value against cases
knowledge_points.worked_example:
command = 'go'
match command:
    case 'go':
        print('Moving')
    case 'stop':
        print('Stopping')
# Moving
The first case whose value equals the subject runs (Python 3.10+).
knowledge_points.practice: Predict output for several subject values, including one that matches no case (nothing prints).

knowledge_points.title: case _ catches everything else
knowledge_points.worked_example:
code = 404
match code:
    case 200:
        print('OK')
    case 404:
        print('Not found')
    case _:
        print('Other')
# Not found
_ matches any value, like a final else; it must come last.
knowledge_points.practice: Add a catch-all case; predict output for unmatched values.

knowledge_points.title: Several values in one case with |
knowledge_points.worked_example:
answer = 'yes'
match answer:
    case 'y' | 'yes':
        print('OK')
    case 'n' | 'no':
        print('Cancelled')
    case _:
        print('Please answer y or n')
# OK
knowledge_points.practice: Combine cases using |; predict which case handles each input.

knowledge_points.title: Only one case runs: rewriting an elif chain as match
knowledge_points.worked_example:
if day == 6 or day == 7: ... elif day == 1: ... else: ...
# becomes case 6 | 7: / case 1: / case _:
There is no fall-through: after a case runs, the match is finished.
knowledge_points.practice: Convert elif chains to match (and back); spot which elif chains cannot be converted because they test ranges.

topics.title: match with capture patterns and guards
topics.summary: Capture the matched value in a name, add if guards to cases, and avoid the bare-name trap that matches everything.

knowledge_points.title: A bare name captures the value
knowledge_points.worked_example:
match n:
    case 0:
        print('zero')
    case other:
        print('got', other)
# n = 5 prints: got 5
A name in a case matches anything and binds the value to that name.
knowledge_points.practice: Predict output and the value bound to the capture name.

knowledge_points.title: Guards: case x if condition
knowledge_points.worked_example:
n = -3
match n:
    case 0:
        print('zero')
    case x if x < 0:
        print('negative')
    case _:
        print('positive')
# negative
The case applies only when the pattern matches and the guard is True.
knowledge_points.practice: Write guarded cases for a classification task; predict which case runs.

knowledge_points.title: The constant trap: a bare name never compares
knowledge_points.worked_example:
colour = 'green'
RED = 'red'
match colour:
    case 'blue':
        print('cold')
    case RED:
        print('warm')   # runs for 'green' too!
case RED captures instead of comparing; use the literal 'red'. A capture case that is not last is rejected: SyntaxError: name capture 'RED' makes remaining patterns unreachable.
knowledge_points.practice: Predict surprising output from bare-name cases; fix them with literals.

topics.title: Repeating with while
topics.summary: Write a while loop with a counter, trace it iteration by iteration, and recognise loops that run zero times.

knowledge_points.title: while repeats its block while the condition is True
knowledge_points.worked_example:
n = 1
while n <= 3:
    print(n)
    n += 1
print('done')
# 1
# 2
# 3
# done
knowledge_points.practice: Predict the output of counter loops; write a loop that prints a given sequence.

knowledge_points.title: Tracing a loop with a table
knowledge_points.worked_example:
i = 0
total = 0
while i < 3:
    total += i
    i += 1
# i: 0 1 2 3   total: 0 0 1 3
Write one row per check of the condition.
knowledge_points.practice: Fill in trace tables for short while loops.

knowledge_points.title: The condition is checked before every pass, so a loop can run zero times
knowledge_points.worked_example:
n = 10
while n < 5:
    print(n)
    n += 1
print('after')
# after
knowledge_points.practice: Predict how many times loops run, including zero.

knowledge_points.title: Counting down
knowledge_points.worked_example:
n = 3
while n > 0:
    print(n)
    n -= 1
print('Liftoff!')
knowledge_points.practice: Write countdown loops for given ranges; reorder lines into a working countdown.

topics.title: Infinite loops and off-by-one errors
topics.summary: Diagnose while loops that never stop or run one time too many or too few, and fix them.

knowledge_points.title: No update means the loop never ends
knowledge_points.worked_example:
n = 1
while n <= 3:
    print(n)
# prints 1 forever: n never changes. Stop the program with the Stop button, then add n += 1.
knowledge_points.practice: Fix loops with a missing update; predict whether a loop terminates.

knowledge_points.title: Updates in the wrong direction or inside an if
knowledge_points.practice: Find the reason each loop never ends and fix it.

knowledge_points.title: Off by one: < vs <= and where the counter starts
knowledge_points.worked_example:
i = 0
while i <= 5:
    print('*')
    i += 1
# 6 stars, not 5: 0..5 is six values. Use i < 5, or start at 1.
knowledge_points.practice: Count how many times loops run; choose the condition that runs exactly n times.

knowledge_points.title: Stepping past an != target
knowledge_points.worked_example:
n = 1
while n != 10:
    n += 2
# 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, ... never equals 10. Use n < 10 when stepping by more than 1.
knowledge_points.practice: Decide which loops terminate; fix != conditions that can be skipped over.

topics.title: Looping until something happens
topics.summary: Write while loops whose number of passes is not known in advance: grow or shrink a value until a target, and take numbers apart digit by digit.

knowledge_points.title: Loop until a target, counting the passes
knowledge_points.worked_example:
balance = 100
years = 0
while balance < 200:
    balance *= 1.1
    years += 1
print(years)  # 8
knowledge_points.practice: Predict or compute the number of passes for growth problems; write such a loop.

knowledge_points.title: Halving until small
knowledge_points.worked_example:
n = 100
steps = 0
while n > 1:
    n //= 2
    steps += 1
print(steps)  # 6
knowledge_points.practice: Trace halving and doubling loops; give the final values.

knowledge_points.title: Digit loops with % 10 and // 10
knowledge_points.worked_example:
n = 4096
total = 0
while n > 0:
    total += n % 10
    n //= 10
print(total)  # 19
% 10 takes the last digit, // 10 removes it.
knowledge_points.practice: Write loops that sum, count or reverse the digits of a number.

knowledge_points.title: After the loop, the variable holds the value that stopped it
knowledge_points.worked_example:
n = 1
while n < 50:
    n *= 3
print(n)  # 81, the first value that is not < 50
knowledge_points.practice: Predict the variable's value after the loop ends.

topics.title: Reading input until a stop value
topics.summary: Write sentinel loops that keep reading input until a special value, using a priming read so the stop value is never processed.

knowledge_points.title: Keep reading until the user types 0
knowledge_points.worked_example:
total = 0
n = int(input('Number (0 to stop): '))
while n != 0:
    total += n
    n = int(input('Number (0 to stop): '))
print('Total:', total)
knowledge_points.practice: Predict the output for a given sequence of typed inputs; write a sentinel loop that counts entries.

knowledge_points.title: Why read once before the loop
knowledge_points.worked_example:
n = 0
while n != 0:          # never runs: n starts at the sentinel
    ...
The priming read gets a real value to test; the read at the end of the body gets the next one.
knowledge_points.practice: Fix sentinel loops that never run, that add the sentinel to the total, or that skip the first value.

knowledge_points.title: Text sentinels
knowledge_points.worked_example:
cmd = input('> ')
while cmd != 'quit':
    print('You said', cmd)
    cmd = input('> ')
print('Bye')
knowledge_points.practice: Write echo-style loops ending on a word; predict output for typed sequences.

topics.title: Asking again until the input is valid
topics.summary: Re-prompt until the user enters an acceptable value and build a guess-the-number loop.

knowledge_points.title: Re-prompt while the value is out of range
knowledge_points.worked_example:
n = int(input('Pick 1-10: '))
while n < 1 or n > 10:
    print('Try again')
    n = int(input('Pick 1-10: '))
print('You picked', n)
knowledge_points.practice: Predict output for a sequence of typed inputs; write a validation loop for a given range.

knowledge_points.title: Write the 'invalid' condition by negating the valid one
knowledge_points.worked_example:
valid: 1 <= n <= 10
loop while: not (1 <= n <= 10)   # same as n < 1 or n > 10
A common bug is n < 1 and n > 10, which is never True.
knowledge_points.practice: Choose or write the loop condition for described valid inputs; fix and-instead-of-or bugs.

knowledge_points.title: A guessing-game loop
knowledge_points.practice: Write the loop from a spec; predict output for a sequence of guesses; extend it to count guesses.

topics.title: Repeating a block n times with for
topics.summary: Use for i in range(n) to repeat a block a fixed number of times and know which values the loop variable takes.

knowledge_points.title: Repeat a block n times
knowledge_points.worked_example:
for i in range(3):
    print('Hip hip hooray!')
# printed 3 times
The indented block is the loop body, as with if.
knowledge_points.practice: Write a loop that prints a line a given number of times; count how many lines a loop prints.

knowledge_points.title: The loop variable takes 0, 1, ..., n - 1
knowledge_points.worked_example:
for i in range(4):
    print(i)
# 0
# 1
# 2
# 3
range(4) starts at 0 and stops before 4.
knowledge_points.practice: Predict the values printed; give the last value of the loop variable.

knowledge_points.title: What repeats and what runs once
knowledge_points.worked_example:
for i in range(2):
    print('in loop', i)
print('after loop')
# in loop 0
# in loop 1
# after loop
knowledge_points.practice: Predict output when lines are indented differently; reorder lines (Parsons) for a target output.

knowledge_points.title: Name the loop variable, or use _ when it is unused
knowledge_points.practice: Choose a suitable loop-variable name; identify loops where the variable is unused.

topics.title: Computing with the loop variable
topics.summary: Use the loop variable inside the body to compute values, number output from 1, and predict its value during and after the loop.

knowledge_points.title: Compute something from i on each pass
knowledge_points.practice: Predict output of loops that compute from i; write a loop that prints a table of values.

knowledge_points.title: Numbering from 1 with i + 1
knowledge_points.practice: Write loops whose output is numbered from 1; fix loops that start numbering at 0.

knowledge_points.title: Changing i inside the body does not change the next pass
knowledge_points.worked_example:
for i in range(3):
    print(i)
    i = 10
# 0 1 2: each pass takes the next value from range, ignoring the assignment.
knowledge_points.practice: Predict output of loops that reassign the loop variable.

knowledge_points.title: After the loop, i keeps its last value
knowledge_points.worked_example:
for i in range(3):
    pass
print(i)  # 2
If the range is empty the body never runs and i is never assigned.
knowledge_points.practice: Predict the loop variable's value after loops, including empty ones (NameError).

topics.title: Looping over the characters of a string
topics.summary: Use for ch in text to visit each character of a string, and count or report characters that match a test.

knowledge_points.title: for visits each character in order
knowledge_points.worked_example:
for ch in 'cat':
    print(ch)
# c
# a
# t
A string is a sequence, so for can walk through it like a range.
knowledge_points.practice: Predict output for short words, including spaces and punctuation, which are characters too.

knowledge_points.title: Count characters that pass a test
knowledge_points.practice: Write loops that count a given character; trace the counter.

knowledge_points.title: for ch in text vs for i in range(n)
knowledge_points.practice: Choose which loop produces a target output; fix a loop that iterates over the wrong thing.

topics.title: Making a decision on every pass
topics.summary: Put if/elif/else inside a for loop to treat each value differently, up to FizzBuzz.

knowledge_points.title: An if inside the loop runs on every pass
knowledge_points.practice: Predict output of loops with an if in the body; write a loop that prints only multiples of 3.

knowledge_points.title: Several branches per pass
knowledge_points.practice: Trace which branch runs on each pass; fill a trace table.

knowledge_points.title: FizzBuzz: order the tests carefully
knowledge_points.practice: Write FizzBuzz-style programs from a spec; fix versions with the tests in the wrong order.

topics.title: Choosing between for and while
topics.summary: Convert counting loops between for and while, and choose for when the number of passes is known and while when it is not.

knowledge_points.title: The same counting loop written two ways
knowledge_points.worked_example:
for i in range(3):
    print(i)
# same output as
i = 0
while i < 3:
    print(i)
    i += 1
knowledge_points.practice: Convert loops between for and while; reorder lines into an equivalent while loop.

knowledge_points.title: Known count: for. Unknown count: while.
knowledge_points.worked_example:
Print 10 rows -> for row in range(10)
Keep doubling until over 1000 -> while n <= 1000
knowledge_points.practice: Pick the more natural loop for described tasks.

knowledge_points.title: A for loop cannot forget its update
knowledge_points.worked_example:
i = 0
while i < 5:
    print(i)
# infinite: the update is missing
for i in range(5): print(i)  -- range advances i for you.
knowledge_points.practice: Fix buggy while counters by rewriting them as for loops.

topics.title: range(start, stop): choosing where to start and stop
topics.summary: Use range(start, stop) to loop over any run of whole numbers, remembering that stop is excluded.

knowledge_points.title: range(start, stop) begins at start
knowledge_points.worked_example:
for i in range(2, 5):
    print(i)
# 2
# 3
# 4
knowledge_points.practice: Predict the numbers produced by range(start, stop).

knowledge_points.title: Stop is excluded: 1 to n inclusive is range(1, n + 1)
knowledge_points.worked_example:
n = 5
for i in range(1, n + 1):
    print(i)
# 1 2 3 4 5
